newsitem.title: CHINA: Biggest China film maker to list despite troubles.
newsitem.headline: Biggest China film maker to list despite troubles.

text.p: China's biggest domestic producer of film plans to list this year and is gearing up to compete with international giants, Eastman Kodak Co of the U.S. and Japan's Fuji Photo Film Co, state media said on Sunday.
China Lucky Film Corp is determined to boost sales despite losing market share to foreign manufacturers, the China Daily Business Weekly said.
"We are confident of rooting a strong position in the Chinese market," the newspaper quoted one company executive as saying.

The company plans to list on a domestic stock market this year, it quoted Li Yaochang, manager of Lucky's import and export department, as saying. He declined to give further details of the planned listing.
Lucky's film sales soared 52 percent in the first five months of this year while photographic paper sales grew 7.9 percent and foreign exchange earnings rose 26 percent, the newspaper said.
Lucky aims to earn $10 million in foreign exchange in 1997, from $9.1 million last year. The company, which has a 20 percent market share, saw sales rise 20 percent last year, Li said.
Lucky was open to setting up a joint venture with a foreign partner and had been contacted by foreign firms, he said.
However, Lucky insisted it be the controlling share-holder, that technology be transferred to the venture and that it retain its Lucky brand name, the only remaining domestic brand, he said.

Eastman Kodak has reportedly been in talks with Lucky and other Chinese film makers on setting up a joint venture to manufacture its film in China, thus eliminating high import tariffs. Fuji already occupies about 48 percent of the China market.

Kodak and Fuji have set up developing shops across China in a move that sharply eroded Lucky's market share, and Lucky is preparing to open 1,000 such franchise stores nationwide, the Business Weekly said.
